description: Scaffold for γγ → qq̄ SDP categorical crossing-budget derivation. H_2 demo confirms σ_0³ has tr_M ≈ 0.73 at q_0 (not 1). H_3 skeleton outlines the 6-dim NF basis + 3 Wedderburn blocks (dims 1, 2, 1). Full SDP solve deferred to follow-up — uses joint_tower_sdp_solver_v2.py (PR #444 Phase 3b) infrastructure.

h3_skeleton_outline.expected_T_w_for_proton_pair: B_3 closure σ_0 σ_1⁻¹ σ_0 σ_1⁻¹ σ_0 σ_1⁻¹ + ud-half + gluon corrections
h3_skeleton_outline.open_question: Does the SDP UNIQUELY pick out 11 crossings, or are there alternative PSD-feasible budgets at H_3? probe_proton_crossing_budget.py shows the answer is 'yes, 11 is uniquely close to AME but other budgets are PSD-feasible too' — so the SDP is not strict enough; an additional constraint (e.g., minimal tr_M complement) is needed to pick out 11 categorically.

path_forward: 1. Run joint_tower_sdp_solver_v2.py with γγ→qq̄ ansatz at H_3

caveats: This is a scaffold, not a complete γγ→qq̄ SDP solve. The full pipeline requires LR-embedding from H_2 (γγ) into H_3 (qq̄ with substrate), then H_3 (qq̄) into H_n (multi-quark hadron). PR #444's joint_tower_sdp_solver_v2 + R4 cross-level consistency provides the SDP infrastructure; wiring γγ as the seed is the deep work.

probe_proton_crossing_budget.py showed PSD-feasible alternatives to the 11-crossing budget exist (different n_b3, n_gluon combinations are also PSD); the SDP needs an additional constraint (e.g., MINIMAL tr_M complement) to uniquely pick the 11-crossing canonical T_w.
